title: When to Fine-Tune, and a Production-Readiness Plan
summary: Prompting, retrieval and fine-tuning solve different problems at very different costs. This lesson gives a decision framework based on failure analysis, break-even arithmetic and total cost of ownership, then closes the module with a production-readiness checklist and a scoring method.
objectives: Classify failures into knowledge, behaviour and capability problems and pick the cheapest fix for each
Estimate the expected quality gain of each intervention from failure shares and fix rates
Compute the break-even volume and payback time for a fine-tune, including maintenance
Explain why retrieval beats fine-tuning for changing or permissioned knowledge
Score a feature against a production-readiness checklist and set launch gates
prerequisites: You should have met prompting ([Anatomy of a Prompt](/learn/prompt-and-context/prompt-anatomy)), RAG ([How RAG Works](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/rag-architecture)) and the idea of parameter-efficient fine-tuning ([LoRA and QLoRA](/learn/training-and-adaptation/peft-lora)). The cost formulas come from [Choosing and Routing Models](/learn/production-systems/model-routing), and error analysis from [Error Analysis](/learn/evaluation/error-analysis).
